newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to grant loans to cattle breeders.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to grant loans to cattle breeders.

text.p: Croatia will this year grant 481 million kuna in loans to cattle breeders to boost meat production, a government minister said on Monday.
"We shall start soon with a test loan for 3,200 heifers by granting 2,500 kuna to farmers for each heifer," Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic told a news conference.
The government planned to back the raising of 25,000 heifers over the year, and it would also cover the costs of rearing pigs, sheep and goats, Dominikovic said.
Funds would come from foreign loans, the Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the government's Agricultural Development Fund.
Individual loans would be granted at slightly under nine percent a year for four years with a grace period of one to two years, Dominikovic said.
To ease access by farmers to these funds, loans would be handled by state-owned Postal Bank (HPB), with branches in virtually every village".
"The aim is to provide farmers with money ahead of spring sowing and to avoid situations when they are forced to sell too young cattle for slaughter," Dominikovic said.
